Young Guns 1988 - An edgy Western Classic

3 May 2023 · RewindZone Archive

Oh boy, let me tell you about the epic 1988 western movie "Young Guns"! This classic flick has stood the test of time, and for good reason. With a cast of up-and-coming actors, an edgy rock soundtrack, and some seriously cool shootouts, "Young Guns" is a wild ride from start to finish.

What's truly impressive about "Young Guns" is how it manages to balance gritty realism with the kind of over-the-top action that makes westerns so exciting. The cast is phenomenal, with Emilio Estevez stealing the show as the charismatic and unpredictable Billy the Kid. And let's not forget Kiefer Sutherland, Lou Diamond Phillips, and Charlie Sheen, who all deliver memorable performances as well.‌

But don't just take my word for it. "Young Guns" was a huge box office success, raking in over $45 million in its theatrical run. And it's not hard to see why - the movie was made on a relatively modest budget of $13 million, so it turned a pretty sweet profit for the studio.

Even if you're not a fan of westerns, "Young Guns" is worth checking out. The action scenes are top-notch, with some seriously impressive gunfights that will keep you on the edge of your seat. And the music! The soundtrack is packed with hits from some of the biggest rock bands of the era, including Jon Bon Jovi and Guns N' Roses. It's the perfect complement to the film's modern, edgy vibe.‌

But what really sets "Young Guns" apart is its willingness to explore the complexity of its characters. Sure, they may be outlaws, but the movie doesn't simply paint them as one-dimensional villains. Instead, we see them grappling with their pasts and their choices, and we're left to question whether they're truly bad people or just products of their circumstances.‌

All in all, "Young Guns" is an absolute classic that deserves to be remembered as one of the great westerns of all time. If you haven't seen it yet, do yourself a favor and give it a watch. You won't be disappointed.
